analysis.summary: Live `npm audit --json` confirms all nine named transitives (brace-expansion, flatted, js-yaml, minimatch, nanoid, picomatch, postcss, rollup, ws) are present at vulnerable versions, each high, each with a non-breaking `fixAvailable: true` — so `npm audit fix` without `--force` clears exactly this list. Remaining findings after the fix are precisely the majors this plan defers: vitest/@vitest/ui (critical, #16), sharp (high, #17), and vite/vite-node/esbuild (deferred to 2.2/#26).
analysis.details: Audit metadata: 19 findings (3 critical, 12 high, 3 moderate, 1 low). The nine target packages all resolve via non-major range updates, so no direct dependency in package.json needs a major bump for this wave. Acceptance is: audit high count for these transitives is 0 with only vite/vitest/sharp-class majors remaining, and `npm run test:run` stays at or above the recorded pass rate. Because vitest (1.0.4) and sharp (0.34.5) majors remain vulnerable after this fix, this issue is the gate for #16 and, in practice, the first write to package.json/package-lock.json of the wave.
